findings.message: Stale task error overrides verified success on real pipeline data. The live run-state.json for project-workflows-001 carries tasks[verify_ui] with a stale CalledProcessError from an earlier superstep together with result.ui_packet, values.ui_packet, a hash-verified passed packet and a 'passed' event; server/projects.ts:614 projects that node as 'failed'. This follows the README's literal precedence rule and never fabricates success, but it renders a passed verification as failed until the next checkpoint. Projecting error-plus-evidence as 'paused' (contradictory evidence) would better match the contract.

Graph attempt is inferred from the maximum 'Attempt N' text in events (server/projects.ts:582-583, 610) rather than the packet registry. The real run's events reach 'Attempt 3' before numbering resets, so verify_ui would display graph attempt 3 while its only registered result is attempt 1. The UI labels the mismatch, but the number is not backed by any registered packet.

RunStore.listRuns (server/projects.ts:320-347) fully loads, parses and hash-verifies every registered packet of every run on each list request with no caching; cost is bounded by the byte limits but grows with runs x packets x packet size.

projectWorkerResult (server/projects.ts:660) forwards raw.error unredacted when the gate passed but the raw result status is 'failed'; only summary and gate reasons go through redactPaths. The current producer never writes that combination, so the leak is latent.

The adapter never emits result_reused events because the persisted export has no explicit reuse signal (reuse from the failure drill lives only in failure-report.json), so live runs always show 'No reuse evidence recorded'. The viewer states the absence explicitly; accepted as the adapter's documented open assumption.

The pre-existing root Playwright suite (tests/graph, document-failure, edit-recovery, locations) is not part of the policy check set, so it ran only in the UI worker's own worktree at commit b72eacc, not against the combined candidate. Policy scoping choice, not a candidate defect.
